macus_build: release, Packaging/install-local.sh into an isolated prefix, ad hoc virtualization signing
crash_injection: Test-only start_post() appended to the guest /etc/conf.d/incusd through a privileged Incus container with the guest root mounted. Each incusd launch consumed one count from /var/lib/tama-acceptance/crashes and sent SIGABRT 1 s after start, so the Go runtime dumped goroutines to stderr and exited. The hook, counter file and container were removed afterwards and conf.d was restored byte-for-byte from its backup.

runs.name: fresh_start
runs.note: incusd writes its log both to --logfile and to stderr, so incusd.err also carries the regular log.

runs.name: single_crash_recovered_in_guest
runs.finding: A 60-line stderr tail of the Go dump held only the last goroutine and registers. The guard now also copies the first 30 lines of the last crash (SIGABRT: abort, crashing goroutine). The updated guard was copied into the guest by sha256 before the next run.

runs.name: persistent_crash_fails_fast_after_one_host_restart
runs.error_message: Incus crashed during guest boot and the guest's bounded restarts were exhausted (code incus_crashed). One automatic guest restart was already tried. The incusd log tail is in serial.log. Disks and Incus data were kept. Inspect serial.log, then run macus runtime stop --force and macus start.

runs.name: crash_recovered_by_host_restart
runs.finding: OpenRC rc.log showed the recovery shutdown was graceful but logged 'incusd failed to stop' and then 'tama-storage failed to stop', so the ZFS pool was not exported. The guard now zaps a crashed incusd when it gives up; on the repeat run incusd no longer blocked shutdown, but zpool export still failed with "cannot unmount '/var/lib/incus': pool or dataset is busy". The pool imported cleanly on every following boot.

runs.name: storage_stop_after_crash
runs.diagnosis: A test-only stop_pre in /etc/conf.d/tama-storage dumped state at storage stop. Clean shutdown: only tama-data/metadata mounted at /var/lib/incus. After a crash: tmpfs /var/lib/incus/devices, shmounts and guestapi still mounted, and an orphaned dnsmasq (parent 1) holding /var/lib/incus/networks/incusbr0/dnsmasq.leases.
runs.fix: storage.sh stop releases a dead incusd's leftovers (TERM/KILL holders under the metadata mount, unmount tmpfs there) after a failed first export, then retries once; never while incusd's daemon is alive and never datasets.

deviations: The appliance was provisioned with payload revision ba33d62b. The guard and later storage.sh were then replaced inside the guest by sha256-verified copy, not by provisioning a second fresh state. The host binary was not rebuilt; later commits change only guest scripts and the embedded payload.
Crashes were injected with SIGABRT from a test hook, not reproduced from the original unexplained crash.
open_findings: A crash while instances run was not exercised; instance processes holding datasets would make the retried export fail as before, and the next boot imports the pool.
